images.section_title: Interpreting Impulse Diagrams by Area Instead of Height
images.image_description: Time-axis diagram with three impulse stems at t=-2, t=1, and t=3. Each stem is centered at the time value and labeled with signed area values above the stem: 2 at t=-2, -1 at t=1, and 4 at t=3. Include a blank tick at t=0 with no stem so the student does not infer an impulse where none exists. Emphasize the area label as the symbolically meaningful quantity; do not encode height semantics or extra graph context.

outline_section.section_title: Interpreting Impulse Diagrams by Area Instead of Height
outline_section.learning_goal: Convert between impulse diagrams and symbolic expressions using impulse areas (including sign) as the interpretive quantity.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Time-axis impulse diagram with at least three stems at different positions, each stem showing distinct signed area labels.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Draw simple centered stems with clear time labels; avoid decorative grid; emphasize stem areas and signs rather than geometric area under height.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given an impulse diagram with labeled areas $A=2$ at $t=1$, $A=-1$ at $t=3$, and no impulse at $t=-2$, identify the equivalent expression.
distractor_plan: Use stem heights as if they were widths in the expression.
Drop negative sign and write all coefficients as absolute values.
Assign areas to shifted steps instead of shifted impulses.
Swap the time locations due to reading left-right inversion.
Add an implicit normalization factor when none exists.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Write the signal expression for the shown impulse diagram: impulses at $t= -1$, $t=0$, and $t=2$ with area labels $3$, $-2$, and $4$, respectively.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce a symbolic expression $3\delta(t+1)-2\delta(t)+4\delta(t-2)$ while preserving sign and time shifts.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from symbolic reading to diagram-based interpretation, adding visual discrimination of sign and location.
solution_step_plan: Read each impulse stem and record its time center $t_0$.
Read the area label attached to each stem as coefficient $A$.
Map each pair to $A\delta(t-t_0)$ and maintain sign.
Order terms consistently for readability, then verify by integrating each term.
practice_variation_axes: Vary number of impulses and include zero-area distractors.
Vary coefficient signs and spacing between impulse times.
Vary location order and whether one impulse is negative.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep image prompts explicit about area labels; avoid requiring the question generator to infer area from stem height.

prompt_blocks.text: Write the signal expression for the shown impulse diagram.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Read each area label as the coefficient of a shifted $\delta$ term and keep the sign with the coefficient: $2$ at $t=-2$ gives $2\delta(t+2)$, $-1$ at $t=1$ gives $-\delta(t-1)$, and $4$ at $t=3$ gives $4\delta(t-3)$.

prompt_blocks.text: Write the signal expression for the shown impulse diagram.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Treat each signed area label as the coefficient of a shifted impulse: $1$ at $t=-3$ gives $\delta(t+3)$, $-2$ at $t=-1$ gives $-2\delta(t+1)$, $3$ at $t=2$ gives $3\delta(t-2)$, and $5$ at $t=4$ gives $5\delta(t-4)$.
